claims.title: The savannas join the trans-Saharan trade
claims.summary: As the Ghana and Mali empires expanded southward, the northern peoples of the region — Senufo and Mandé — were drawn into trans-Saharan commerce, exchanging forest kola nuts for salt, cloth, and gold.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1100-the-savannas-join-the-trans-saharan-trade, claim TL:CIV:event:1100:the-savannas-join-the-trans-saharan-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dyula merchants found northern trading towns
claims.summary: Mandé-speaking Muslim merchants, the Dyula, established trading and Islamic centres such as Kong, Bondoukou, Bouna, and Begho, linking the rainforest to the markets of the Sahel.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1300-dyula-merchants-found-northern-trading-towns, claim TL:CIV:event:1300:dyula-merchants-found-northern-trading-towns, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Seku Watara founds the Empire of Kong
claims.summary: Seku Watara united the Dyula of Kong into a state, often called the Wattara Empire, that grew rich controlling the gold and kola trade and reached into present-day Burkina Faso, Mali, and Ghana.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1710-seku-watara-founds-the-empire-of-kong, claim TL:CIV:event:1710:seku-watara-founds-the-empire-of-kong, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kong expands northward
claims.summary: Under Seku Watara and his kin the empire of Kong extended its reach, conquering toward Bobo-Dioulasso and cementing its dominance over the regional trade routes before central authority weakened after his death about 1745.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1737-kong-expands-northward, claim TL:CIV:event:1737:kong-expands-northward, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Akan states form on the eastern frontier
claims.summary: As the Asante Empire rose in present-day Ghana, Akan groups such as the Abron founded states near the eastern edge of modern Côte d'Ivoire, beginning a long era of Akan migration into the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1690-akan-states-form-on-the-eastern-frontier, claim TL:CIV:event:1690:akan-states-form-on-the-eastern-frontier, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Baoulé migrate under Queen Abla Pokou
claims.summary: By tradition, Queen Abla Pokou broke from the Asante after a succession struggle and led her people west across the Comoé River, founding the Baoulé kingdom around Sakasso — the largest people of modern Côte d'Ivoire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1750-the-baoule-migrate-under-queen-abla-pokou, claim TL:CIV:event:1750:the-baoule-migrate-under-queen-abla-pokou, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Agni kingdoms of Indénié and Sanwi
claims.summary: Other Akan groups fleeing the Asante established the Agni (Anyi) kingdoms of Indénié and Sanwi in the south-east, near the lagoons and the Gold Coast, extending Akan institutions across the forest zone.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1750-the-agni-kingdoms-of-indenie-and-sanwi, claim TL:CIV:event:1750:the-agni-kingdoms-of-indenie-and-sanwi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Earliest recorded French voyage to the coast
claims.summary: French mariners reached the West African coast; over the following centuries European traders worked the shore for ivory, gold, and other goods, giving the Ivory Coast its lasting name, though its surf-bound coast limited permanent contact.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1483-earliest-recorded-french-voyage-to-the-coast, claim TL:CIV:event:1483:earliest-recorded-french-voyage-to-the-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France signs treaties on the lagoon coast
claims.summary: The naval officer Bouët-Willaumez concluded treaties with rulers around Grand-Bassam and Assinie, securing the first durable French trading footholds on the coast of present-day Côte d'Ivoire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1843-france-signs-treaties-on-the-lagoon-coast, claim TL:CIV:event:1843:france-signs-treaties-on-the-lagoon-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France constitutes the colony of Côte d'Ivoire
claims.summary: After protectorate treaties negotiated by Binger and Treich-Laplène, France formally established the colony of Côte d'Ivoire on 10 March 1893, naming Louis-Gustave Binger its first governor.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1893-france-constitutes-the-colony-of-cote-d-ivoire, claim TL:CIV:event:1893:france-constitutes-the-colony-of-cote-d-ivoire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capture of Samori Touré ends northern resistance
claims.summary: The Mandé empire-builder Samori Touré, who had resisted the French for years and sacked Kong, was captured at Guélémou on 29 September 1898 and exiled to Gabon, breaking organised resistance in the savanna.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1898-capture-of-samori-toure-ends-northern-resistance, claim TL:CIV:event:1898:capture-of-samori-toure-ends-northern-resistance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Côte d'Ivoire joins French West Africa
claims.summary: The colony became a constituent territory of the Federation of French West Africa, governed from Dakar, and was developed as a source of cocoa, coffee, and timber for the metropole.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1904-cote-d-ivoire-joins-french-west-africa, claim TL:CIV:event:1904:cote-d-ivoire-joins-french-west-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Head tax and forced labour
claims.summary: France imposed a head tax in 1900 and a forced-labour regime that compelled African men to work without pay on infrastructure and plantations, drawing recruits from the lands later organised as Upper Volta and provoking repeated revolts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1900-head-tax-and-forced-labour, claim TL:CIV:event:1900:head-tax-and-forced-labour, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Houphouët-Boigny founds the African Agricultural Union
claims.summary: Félix Houphouët-Boigny organised African cocoa and coffee planters into the Syndicat Agricole Africain to win them the rights enjoyed by European growers — the start of his rise to political leadership.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1944-houphouet-boigny-founds-the-african, claim TL:CIV:event:1944:houphouet-boigny-founds-the-african, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Forced labour abolished
claims.summary: On a bill closely associated with Houphouët-Boigny, the French parliament abolished forced labour throughout the empire in 1946; the same year he helped found the inter-territorial RDA and its Ivorian party, the PDCI.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1946-forced-labour-abolished, claim TL:CIV:event:1946:forced-labour-abolished, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence under Houphouët-Boigny
claims.summary: After choosing autonomy within the French Community in a 1958 referendum, Côte d'Ivoire became a fully independent republic on 7 August 1960, with Félix Houphouët-Boigny as its first president.

sources.label: Côte d'Ivoire gains independence from France

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-under-houphouet-boigny, claim TL:CIV:event:1960:independence-under-houphouet-boigny, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 'Ivorian miracle'
claims.summary: Liberal, export-led growth built on cocoa and coffee and close ties to France made Côte d'Ivoire one of the most prosperous states in sub-Saharan Africa, with Abidjan a thriving commercial hub.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1960-the-ivorian-miracle, claim TL:CIV:event:1960:the-ivorian-miracle, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Commodity slump ends the boom
claims.summary: A collapse in world cocoa and coffee prices ended the era of rapid growth, leaving heavy debt and rising discontent that would strain the one-party system.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1980-commodity-slump-ends-the-boom, claim TL:CIV:event:1980:commodity-slump-ends-the-boom, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Capital moved to Yamoussoukro
claims.summary: Houphouët-Boigny designated his birthplace, Yamoussoukro, the official political capital, though Abidjan remained the economic and administrative centre.

sources.label: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace of Yamoussoukro

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1983-capital-moved-to-yamoussoukro, claim TL:CIV:event:1983:capital-moved-to-yamoussoukro, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace consecrated
claims.summary: The vast basilica at Yamoussoukro, modelled on St Peter's in Rome and recognised as the largest church in the world, was consecrated by Pope John Paul II amid controversy over its enormous cost.

sources.label: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace of Yamoussoukro
Our Lady of Peace of Yamoussoukro Basilica (1989– )

claims.title: First multiparty election
claims.summary: Under domestic and international pressure Houphouët-Boigny legalised opposition parties and won the country's first multiparty presidential election against the historian Laurent Gbagbo.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1990-first-multiparty-election, claim TL:CIV:event:1990:first-multiparty-election, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Houphouët-Boigny
claims.summary: The country's founding president died in office after more than three decades in power, leaving a celebrated record of stability and growth but no clearly prepared successor.

sources.label: Félix Houphouët-Boigny (1905–1993), first President of Côte d'Ivoire

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1993-death-of-houphouet-boigny, claim TL:CIV:event:1993:death-of-houphouet-boigny, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The politics of 'Ivoirité'
claims.summary: President Bédié promoted 'Ivoirité', a doctrine of authentic Ivorian belonging used to exclude rivals such as Alassane Ouattara and to question the citizenship of northerners and immigrants, deepening a north–south rift.

sources.label: Côte d'Ivoire's Post-Electoral Crisis: Ouattara Rules but Can He Govern?

claims.title: The first coup d'état
claims.summary: General Robert Guéï overthrew President Henri Konan Bédié in the country's first military coup, ending the PDCI's unbroken hold on power since independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-1999-the-first-coup-d-etat, claim TL:CIV:event:1999:the-first-coup-d-etat, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Civil war divides the country
claims.summary: An army mutiny grew into a rebellion that split Côte d'Ivoire between a government-held south and a rebel-held north under the Forces Nouvelles, drawing in French and UN peacekeepers.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-2002-civil-war-divides-the-country, claim TL:CIV:event:2002:civil-war-divides-the-country, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ouagadougou Political Agreement
claims.summary: A peace accord brokered through regional mediation brought rebel leader Guillaume Soro into a unity government and set a path toward reunification and elections, easing the first civil war.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-2007-ouagadougou-political-agreement, claim TL:CIV:event:2007:ouagadougou-political-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Post-election crisis
claims.summary: After the disputed November 2010 runoff, Gbagbo refused to cede to Ouattara; the standoff became open conflict that killed about 3,000 people before pro-Ouattara forces, backed by France and the UN, captured Gbagbo on 11 April 2011.

sources.label: Côte d'Ivoire's Post-Electoral Crisis: Ouattara Rules but Can He Govern?

claims.title: Recovery under Ouattara
claims.summary: Alassane Ouattara took office and presided over a return to rapid growth; he was re-elected in 2015 and won a contested third term in 2020 that opponents argued was unconstitutional.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Ivory Coast: From the Dyula trading empire of Kong and the Baoulé migration under Queen Abla Pokou to French conquest, the cocoa-fuelled 'Ivorian miracle' under Houphouët-Boigny, and the civil wars that tested the nation.", terralore.co/country/CIV/chronicle#ev-2011-recovery-under-ouattara, claim TL:CIV:event:2011:recovery-under-ouattara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
